title: QuickBooks receives each part line at its invoice price, in today's shape
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View', 'Customers — Create & Edit', 'Work Orders — Order Parts' and 'Work Order Lines — Create & Edit'.
  • Use staging with the QuickBooks sandbox connected, and sign in to that QuickBooks sandbox in a second browser window.
  • Have a new category for this test, category A, priced by a new matrix for this test, matrix A, with one cost range ($0.00 and up) whose Default rule is Markup % 35.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses, whose column in matrix A is % Off 10.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, put on tier A for work orders in Edit Customer.
  • Have a new inventory part for this test at your location, in category A, cost $10.00, fixed sell price $12.50.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 1, for customer A, made after customer A's tier was set, with one labor line (line 1), with a tier-priced part in category A at $121.50, the fixed-price part at $12.50 and a part with a typed price of $99.00.
  • Use a desktop browser window at least 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so every column of the page shows.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Invoice.
  3. Open the invoice in the QuickBooks sandbox once it has synced.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens with its three parts.

Step 2:

  • The invoice is created and syncs as today.

Step 3:

  • QuickBooks shows the three part lines at $121.50, $12.50 and $99.00, the same as the ShopView invoice ($121.50 + $12.50 + $99.00 = $233.00).
  • No line in QuickBooks mentions a tier, Manual, Fixed price or a price details text.
